text.tspan: What the flow is constrained by: one invariant for the chain, none for the ring
the clamped chain's invariant algebra is ℚ[E] and it lives on a sphere; the reduced ring's is trivial and it lives on nothing
, 0 independent conserved quantities [proved for the stated N and degree; see panel D]
A. The clamped chain: one invariant, ℚ[E] — the flow is caught on a sphere
the one invariant is the energy, and ℚ[E] is the whole algebra
the single invariant: E = Σ u
a level set of E is a sphere in ℝ
, and the flow never leaves it
no second independent invariant through degree 8 — not E
[proved through degree 8: the invariant algebra is ℚ[E]]
the enstrophy ceiling — and it is what regularises the chain
not an invariant — a bound: whatever the flow does, H stays below the ceiling
red dot: H at t = 50 — 223.48, still rising (measured, RK4)
H is monotone increasing and approaches the ceiling asymptotically; it never crosses it.
E − H falls like 2E/t = 28/t: 0.560 predicted vs 0.523 measured at t = 50
the ceiling is attained exactly when all the energy sits on the top shell,
u = (0, 0, ±√14) — the saturation this approach is climbing toward.
E, equality at the top shell]
E − H against t — log-log, slope −1
B. The reduced ring on ℤ/N: zero conserved quantities — the flow lives on nothing
the contrast: nothing constrains this flow
no level set, no invariant manifold to confine the blow-up:
the ring has no conserved quantity at all, so there is no subtorus to lean on.
nothing — no level set at all
tori — never reached, not even by the chain
N − 1 invariants would be needed for a full torus; the chain reaches 1, the ring 0.
(i) the one symmetry that survives: scaling
(λt), λ > 0: the field is homogeneous of degree 2
a symmetry, not a conserved quantity — it moves the clock and the amplitude together
(ii) the one invariant manifold that survives: the diagonal
q(t) = a/(1 − 3at): blow-up at t = 1/(3a), a = q(0) [exact; measured t*]
the diagonal is a genuine invariant submanifold — but not an invariant:
it is one slice, and on it the flow blows up in finite time, unconstrained.
the blow-up is Cascade.selfSimilar re-derived; its physical enstrophy is infinite.
C. Why it is not a Volterra / Kac–van Moerbeke lattice
every axis is a wall the flow cannot cross
no wall exists for the flow to be trapped behind
the structural test, in normalized variables
a pure square can never become a product x
: every monomial must carry a factor x
A normalization rescales the coordinates; it cannot change which monomials appear.
so no invertible linear change of variables makes the ring a Volterra/KvM lattice;
nor is it Hamiltonian for any log-canonical or constant Poisson structure. (CLOSURE §5.6)
a general nonlinear transformation is left open (the §5.8 conjecture), as is a general Lax pair.
note the count once more: N hyperplanes for Volterra, 0 for the ring when N ≥ 3.
= 0 is not invariant for any k]
D. The honest caveats — read before believing A, B, C
a negative result, reported as one
PROVED, AND ONLY THUS FAR. Polynomial invariants are excluded for degrees ≤ 9 and for the computed N — N = 2..6 to degree 9, N = 7 to degree 8, N = 8..12 to degree 5. “No
invariant at any degree for all N” is a CONJECTURE, not a theorem. (CLOSURE §5.4)
first integrals. Locally every nonvanishing field has one (flow-box straightening), so the null is about polynomial and global invariants
, has no meaningful invariant to count.
EXACT, AND VALIDATED. Fraction RREF over ℚ, cross-checked in sympy, non-existence certified mod two large primes. The engine was validated by recovering the KNOWN
Volterra invariants — a negative result is only as good as its engine. (CLOSURE §5.3)
NOT A DISCOVERY. The diagonal blow-up re-derives the repo's existing Cascade.selfSimilar, whose physical enstrophy is infinite; the repo's overall verdict is negative.
three different things that the surrounding document names alike
a set the flow cannot leave — isotropy, a different notion (CLOSURE
a function constant along the flow — the chain's E; the ring has none
a geometric object of genus 1 — unrelated to either of the above
The clamped chain has one invariant and lives on a sphere; the ring has none and lives on nothing — no tori, and no subtorus confinement to lean on for a blow-up argument. (CLOSURE §5.9)
